text:
alex: seeing control-plane API flaps in eu-north1, multiple auth requests timing out, console sessions dropping. started ~10:05 UTC.
priya: observed elevated 5xx from auth-proxy and routing mesh. dashboards show control-plane DNS errors for controller services.
matt: running quick curl from jump: `curl -v https://controller.eu-north1.redwood.internal/health` -> hangs on name resolution, no A record returned.
sre-oncall-bot: [ALERT] control-plane.dns.eu-north1.nameserver: high SERVFAIL rate (90th percentile) - triggered at 10:08 UTC
janet: console and rollout operations failing because control plane calls to kv-store time out. can we failover control-plane to standby region?
alex: can we *not* do full region failover yet — need to assess state of persistent kv leader. if we flip routing we risk split-brain for deployments.
priya: agree. suggest traffic-shift for API and console to na-west2/ eu-central1 for read operations, keep writes gated. we can use emergency routing policy to route 80% to standby and 20% to degraded cluster for sanity checks.
matt: creating traffic-shift in routing layer now: `redwoodctl route shift --from eu-north1 --to na-west2,eu-central1 --weights 80,20 --kind api,console`
ops-runbook-bot: runbook: CONTROLPLANE_DNS_BLACKHOLE v1.4 — recommended steps: 1) isolate DNS server pool, 2) enable fallback imaging to static upstream, 3) pause config rollouts.
janet: pause config rollouts = done (api: /rollouts paused). stopping any canaries.
alex: attempting controlled DNS fallback: switching pods to use external resolvers and restarting controller agents on nodes with good networking. applying: `kubectl -n controlplane set env daemonset/controller DNS_FALLBACK=8.8.8.8`
matt: restart issued, some controllers came back with resolved endpoints, but KV leader reports increased election churn.
priya: telemetry: auth requests that hit fallback resolvers show higher latency but succeed. console sessions restored for ~60% of users routed to na-west2.
alex: opening ticket with infra networking: likely upstream BGP flap causing selective blackholing of internal zone. tagging netops.
janet: cost note: traffic-shift will increase cross-region egress, approx estimated +$2.4k/day if maintained. logging for finance.
matt: continuing to drain GPU workloads from eu-north1 nodes that depend on control-plane (jobs marked drain: true) to avoid unexpected kills.
sre-oncall-bot: [INFO] incident severity upgraded to SEV2 due to partial region control-plane degradation (10:27 UTC). paging eng-runtime.
alex: eng-runtime, can you hold on rolling any kernel/compile changes in the next 2 hours? we need stable controlplane state. @eng-runtime
janet: next steps: keep ingress fallback active, monitor KV election stability, resume rollouts only after 30m of stable leader and DNS.
priya: will continue monitoring dashboards and post periodic updates every 15m.
janet: if DNS not healthy in 45m, plan B is to failover control-plane VIPs to secondary ASNs and then do controlled region failover.
alex: thanks all — updating incident doc and will post when we start plan B. :thumbsup:
